author: EmuCore - Hub
title: PS2 game hacking & reverse engineering
summary: Xeeynamo gives a long-form tour of Kingdom Hearts II reverse engineering through PCSX2, Cheat Engine, Ghidra, MIPS calling conventions and the open OpenKh project, connecting runtime observation to durable file-format and engine research.

blocks.text: The seventy-five-minute session follows a real preservation-oriented codebase instead of offering disconnected hacking tricks. Runtime behavior can be observed through PCSX2 and Cheat Engine, while Ghidra and a linked MIPS calling-convention reference help interpret executable structure. OpenKh provides the public destination for that knowledge: engine findings and file-format work become inspectable tools rather than notes trapped in one video. Kingdom Hearts II is the concrete subject, but the research loop—observe, hypothesize, disassemble, label, test and document—transfers to other PS2 software.

The creator warns that the opening audio echo lasts until roughly five minutes, and a 2019 toolchain inevitably differs from current releases. Reverse-engineered names and format interpretations can remain provisional until checked against many files and execution paths. The video does not provide copyrighted game assets, nor should viewers obtain them from unlicensed sources; work from personal lawful copies and share only original code or permitted metadata. Read the current OpenKh repository history before treating any function label, offset or parser behavior from the recording as final.
